scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: CPCC: do merge heights follow point distances? Compare with random data

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: each dot on the left is a pair (one in every $3$ drawn), with distance $d_{ij}$ across and cophenetic $c_{ij}$ up; the right shows CPCC of $100$ uniform data sets.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: $N=36$: UPGMA cophenetic matrix $P_c$ vs. proximity matrix $P$

scene-u01-pnew1-437.name: text#437
scene-u01-pnew1-437.text: $CPCC$: the correlation of $d_{ij}$ and $c_{ij}$ (the $M=N(N-1)/2$ upper-triangle entries)

scene-u01-pnew1-438.name: text#438
scene-u01-pnew1-438.text: Three groups: close pairs merge low, far pairs merge high, giving two tidy layers

scene-u01-pnew1-440.name: text#440
scene-u01-pnew1-440.text: Random position hypothesis: UPGMA on $100$ uniform sets

scene-u01-pnew1-466.name: text#466
scene-u01-pnew1-466.text: Uniform data already give CPCC $0.64$ to $0.85$

scene-u01-pnew1-469.name: text#469
scene-u01-pnew1-469.text: Misconception: "CPCC is $0.8$, so the tree is faithful."

scene-u01-pnew1-470.name: text#470
scene-u01-pnew1-470.text: Uniform data with no groups can reach $0.85$ under UPGMA. The source warns that even near $0.9$, UPGMA does not guarantee $P_c$ fits $P$.

scene-u01-pnew1-472.name: text#472
scene-u01-pnew1-472.text: Demo data and numbers computed by code [Added]

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: $\gamma$ and $\tau$ use order only: concordant minus discordant pairs

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left shows the two vectors of Example 16.4 with the sign of $v_{p_i}-v_{c_i}$ above each position; each cell on the right is a pair of positions, same sign concordant, opposite sign discordant.

scene-u01-pnew2-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew2-46.text: Only the denominator differs: $\gamma$ drops pairs that count as neither

scene-u01-pnew2-48.name: text#48
scene-u01-pnew2-48.text: $15$ pairs: $3$ plus–plus and $3$ minus–minus pairs are concordant

scene-u01-pnew2-94.name: text#94
scene-u01-pnew2-94.text: Note: two definitions share the name $\gamma$ [Added]

scene-u01-pnew2-95.name: text#95
scene-u01-pnew2-95.text: The common Goodman–Kruskal $\gamma$ compares order within each vector; Example 16.4 then gives $S_+=4$, $S_-=10$, $\gamma=-0.429$. Check the definition before using a library.

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: One clustering: labels come from the algorithm, so rerun it on random data too

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left shows four-group data at two spreads, colored by $k$-means ($m=4$); the right shows $\hat{\Gamma}_i$ of $100$ uniform data sets after rerunning it.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: $Y(i,j)=1$: the points are in different clusters

scene-u01-pnew3-215.name: text#215
scene-u01-pnew3-215.text: Same $Y$ as in KP02, but the labels are the algorithm's own output

scene-u01-pnew3-218.name: text#218
scene-u01-pnew3-218.text: Covariance $0.1I$: $\hat{\Gamma}=0.5704$, above $99$, rejected; $0.2I$: above only $86$, not rejected

scene-u01-pnew3-220.name: text#220
scene-u01-pnew3-220.text: Random position hypothesis: rerun $k$-means on every uniform set

scene-u01-pnew3-243.name: text#243
scene-u01-pnew3-243.text: Uniform data forced into four groups already give $\hat{\Gamma}$ near $0.6$

scene-u01-pnew3-246.name: text#246
scene-u01-pnew3-246.text: How the spread is read changes the verdict

scene-u01-pnew3-247.name: text#247
scene-u01-pnew3-247.text: Read literally as covariance $0.1I$ (std. dev. about $0.32$), the groups nearly merge and $\hat{\Gamma}=0.559$ is not rejected; read as std. dev. $0.1$ and $0.2$, the results match the source.

steps.label: Cophenetic correlation coefficient
steps.speakerNotes: Three-group CPCC is 0.94, above 100 uniform sets (0.64–0.85); uniform data can also score high, so compare with random.

steps.label: Concordant and discordant pairs
steps.speakerNotes: Example 16.4: signs per position, same sign concordant, opposite discordant, S+=6, S-=9, γ=τ=-0.2; the Goodman–Kruskal definition gives -0.429.

steps.label: Testing a single clustering
steps.speakerNotes: Y uses the algorithm's labels; k-means is rerun on random data; std. dev. 0.1 gives 0.814 (reject), 0.2 gives 0.642, above only 86 (not rejected).
